examples.solution_text:
The two semicircular arcs together have the circumference of one circle of diameter $10$ m. Their diameters are not boundary edges.
$\begin{aligned}P&=18+18+2\times\frac12\times\pi(10)\\&=36+10\pi\\&\approx67.4\text{ m}\end{aligned}$

The dashed radii are inside the shape. Add the base, the two vertical sides and the arc subtending $73.7^\circ$.
$\begin{aligned}l&=\frac{73.7}{360}\times2\pi(15)\\&=\frac{737\pi}{120}\text{ mm}\end{aligned}$
$\begin{aligned}P&=18+12+12+l\\&=42+\frac{737\pi}{120}\\&\approx61.29\text{ mm}\end{aligned}$

examples.derivation: The closed outline contains three rectangle sides and an outward semicircle; the dashed diameter is internal. P = 8 + 8 + 4 + π(4)/2 = 20 + 2π ≈ 26.3 cm. The composite boundary cannot use the sector formula.

The quadrant has radius 5 m. The bottom boundary is 7 + 5 m, and the shared vertical radius is internal. P = 7 + 5 + 7 + 5 + 2π(5)/4 = 24 + 2.5π ≈ 31.85 m, following the supplied composite-quadrant example.

The diagram shows the square remaining outside a removed quadrant centred at the lower-left corner. Only the top, right side and concave quarter-circle arc count. P = 6 + 6 + 2π(6)/4 = (12 + 3π) cm. This uses the supplied boundary-addition and quarter-circle methods without introducing another skill.
Both outward semicircles have diameter 10 m and together contribute 10π m. P = 18 + 18 + 10π ≈ 67.4 m. Combining the equal arcs matches the supplied athletics-track and multiple-semicircle tasks.

The large diameter is 12 cm and the cutout diameter is 6 cm. The inward small arc and outward large arc both belong to the boundary; the dashed 6 cm section does not. P = 6 + π(12)/2 + π(6)/2 = (6 + 9π) cm, matching the supplied semicircular-cutout task.

The endpoints (−9,12) and (9,12) are each 15 units from O. Their central angle is approximately 73.7398°, consistent with the stated 73.7°. Using the required displayed angle, l = (73.7/360)2π(15) = 737π/120 mm. P = 18 + 12 + 12 + l ≈ 61.29 mm, using the supplied general-angle composite method.
The concentric semicircular arcs have radii 6.5 m and 2.5 m. Each straight end is 6.5 − 2.5 = 4 m. P = 4 + 4 + π(6.5) + π(2.5) = 8 + 9π ≈ 36.27 m, matching the supplied semicircular-ring task.
